title: Optical Telescopes: Refractors and Reflectors
welcome_lead: Lenses vs mirrors — the two main optical designs.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: refractors, reflectors and resolving power.
final_note: Bigger apertures gather more light and resolve finer detail.

walkthroughs.body_html: Refractors use lenses but suffer chromatic aberration. Big lenses sag under their own weight, so the largest practical refractor (Yerkes, 1897) is 1 m across.
Reflectors use a parabolic primary mirror — no chromatic aberration and easier to support from behind. Almost all large modern telescopes (Keck, VLT) are reflectors.
The Rayleigh criterion gives angular resolution about 1.22 lambda/D in radians. Doubling aperture halves the smallest detail you can see, at the same wavelength.
